decision: Replace the chronological career-opening candidate with a reader-first central-event opening test.
reason: Human review identified a deeper failure mode: even coherent character arcs can read as flat if sentences, scenes and chapters do not create causal necessity for the reader. The novel needs a strong public incident that generates multiple rational positions and makes each later scene necessary.
supersedes: opening architecture driven primarily by career chronology
the assumption that ordinary-life realism alone can carry the opening
retains: Luo Cheng as a strong possible first focal anchor
Campbell as hidden longitudinal character structure
frozen historical ledger and no writeback
new_nonnegotiable: Every sentence must have a reader-facing function or be deleted.
Every scene must change state and cause later action.
Every conspicuous setup enters a payoff registry.
Each chapter must pay off at least one earlier setup before taking on major new narrative debt.
Characters enter because the central incident reaches their role, information, authority or interest; never because the ensemble roster needs coverage.
Technical findings matter only when they alter decisions, power, workload, trust, money, reputation or responsibility.
next_gate: Draft only Chapter2 of the central-event opening from the Chapter1 final discovery. Do not resume the old chronological sequence until the central-event architecture is judged inferior by human review.
